evals.prompt: Our Next.js repo ships on Vercel and we have no Algolia account. Get Algolia set up for this project and prove search works.
evals.expected_output: Point at the Vercel integration entrypoint and its live guide for provisioning, then own the Algolia part: map the injected variables, and validate with a query using the search-only key.
expectations: Names 'vercel integration add algolia' as the entrypoint and defers plans, terms, billing, team and project mechanics to the Vercel docs or 'vercel integration guide algolia --framework <framework>' instead of reproducing a Vercel CLI tutorial
Does NOT use 'algolia auth signup' or 'algolia application create' on this path
Does not hardcode plan IDs, region codes or metadata keys from memory
Maps the injected names to what the Algolia CLI reads: ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID from ALGOLIA_APP_ID, and ALGOLIA_API_KEY from the write or search key depending on the operation
Validates with 'algolia search ... -o json' using the SEARCH key and reads nbHits rather than treating a clean exit as success
Reports what the CLI query returned rather than claiming the deployed app's search is working

evals.prompt: Our Algolia resource is already connected to this Vercel project and the ALGOLIA_APP_ID, ALGOLIA_SEARCH_API_KEY and ALGOLIA_WRITE_API_KEY are available. Wire it up and show me a search against our existing 'products' index.
evals.expected_output: Nothing to provision. Map the variables, search the existing index read-only, and report the result.
expectations: Provisions nothing — no 'vercel integration add', no new Algolia application, no standalone signup
Exports ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID from ALGOLIA_APP_ID and ALGOLIA_API_KEY from the search key for the query
Queries the existing 'products' index rather than creating an example index
Writes no records: no 'objects import', no 'indices clear', no 'indices delete'
Reports the actual nbHits instead of asserting success

evals.prompt: Add Algolia search to our Vercel-hosted Next.js app. Put the credentials where the client-side search component can read them.
evals.expected_output: Only the app ID and the search-only key become public; the write key stays server-side.
expectations: Exposes ONLY the application ID and the search-only key to the browser
Keeps ALGOLIA_WRITE_API_KEY server-side: no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix and no entry in a public config block
Derives the public values from the raw injected names rather than hardcoding key values
Merges into any existing next.config.js and keeps its wrappers rather than replacing the file, or follows whatever mechanism the project already uses for public config
Does not present the next.config.js snippet as the only possible mechanism for non-Next.js frameworks

evals.prompt: I just got a fresh empty Algolia application through the Vercel Marketplace and the credentials are set up. Load some example data and prove search works before we build UI.
evals.expected_output: Additive ndjson import into a new, clearly-example index using the write key, then a search with the search-only key.
expectations: Writes ndjson — one JSON object per line, not a JSON array — with an objectID on each record, and creates the file before referencing it with -F
Imports into a new, clearly-example index name
Does NOT run 'algolia indices clear' or 'algolia indices delete' to prepare
Passes '-w' to the import so the validation query does not race indexing
Uses the WRITE key for the import and the SEARCH key for the validation query
Tells the user the example index name so they can remove it later

evals.prompt: Our Vercel-connected Algolia app already has a 'catalog' index with about 400 products. The search from our app returns nothing. Figure out whether the credentials are the problem.
evals.expected_output: Read-only diagnosis against the existing index. Do not seed data to manufacture hits.
expectations: Queries the existing 'catalog' index with the search-only key — does NOT import demo data to get something to query
Compares nbHits to the ~400 records the user expects rather than accepting any response as success
Distinguishes a failed request (proves nothing, including access) from a successful request returning 0 hits (credentials and index access are fine)
Does NOT claim a missing or misnamed index returns zero hits
Does not propose re-provisioning or deleting environment variables as a first remedy

evals.prompt: Because of a name clash our Algolia resource was connected with a prefix, so the configured variables are ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_APP_ID, ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_SEARCH_API_KEY and ALGOLIA2_ALGOLIA_WRITE_API_KEY. Get a validation query running.
evals.expected_output: Use the configured names verbatim, mapped to the ones the Algolia CLI reads.
expectations: Uses the exact prefixed names as given rather than the unprefixed defaults
Does NOT invent a different transformation of the names, such as dropping the second ALGOLIA_ segment
Still supplies ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID and ALGOLIA_API_KEY to the Algolia CLI, sourced from the prefixed variables
Applies the same prefixed names consistently anywhere it maps public browser values
Does NOT re-provision or reconnect the resource to obtain unprefixed names

evals.prompt: Set Algolia up for our Vercel project. We only care about production — preview and development don't matter to us.
evals.expected_output: Target production explicitly on every environment-scoped command; do not silently work against a different environment.
expectations: Targets production explicitly wherever an environment must be named, and uses the same one consistently
Does NOT quietly operate against development, and does not assert a universal default environment on the user's behalf
Sends the environment command syntax and flags to the Vercel docs rather than reproducing them as a tutorial
Still maps the variables and validates with a search-only-key query

evals.prompt: Our Next.js app is deployed on Vercel. We've had a standalone Algolia account for two years with our 'products' index and our own API keys in our secret manager. Add autocomplete to the header.
evals.expected_output: The standalone application stays standalone. Vercel hosting alone is not a reason to provision a duplicate; this is UI work.
expectations: Keeps the existing standalone Algolia application — does NOT provision a Vercel Marketplace resource
Does NOT run 'vercel integration add algolia' just because the app is hosted on Vercel
Uses the credentials already in the user's secret manager
Routes the autocomplete implementation to instantsearch, offering 'npx skills add algolia/skills --skill instantsearch' if it is not installed rather than requiring it up front
If it raises the Marketplace option at all, frames it as an explicit migration choice, not a step in this task
